reference.source: Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Wrists inward rash with tick: spotted fever
Eschar plus forest fever: scrub typhus
No wall, fried egg, cold agglutinins: Mycoplasma
reference.pathophysiology: Endothelial invasion vasculitides skin into rash while Orientia eschars necrose mite feeding sites; chlamydial elementary bodies survive extracellularly to seed new cells, and wall less mycoplasmas fuse membranes triggering cold agglutinin cross reaction.
additionalDifferentials: RMSF versus meningococcaemia by palms, soles and tick history
Scrub versus murine typhus by eschar and OXK
Mycoplasma versus chlamydial pneumonia by bullae and agglutinins
additionalInvestigations: Weil-Felix with eschar hunt and scrub IgM
Genital NAAT with LGV PCR in groove sign disease
Cold agglutinins with Mycoplasma PCR in walking pneumonia
